page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating on an arm64 architecture, this instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, alongside 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a 15 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory performance, with uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching a top-tier 384.64 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 170.56 GB/sec. Multi-core processing is highly efficient, as evidenced by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21489.0 and a strong software compilation score of 49333.0. Database operations perform exceptionally well, scoring in the top tier on Passmark database tests with 46924.96 points and delivering a strong 70.72 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. However, the instance exhibits a tradeoff in large-scale machine learning workloads, showing weak performance in prompt processing for 70B parameter models at 5.91 tokens per second.

The c8gd.8xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy and storage-dependent workloads due to its ARM-based architecture and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage. By bundling 1900 GB of NVMe SSD directly with 32 dedicated cores, it eliminates the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput local operations. This resource density makes the instance highly suitable for database hosting, multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput web serving, and localized data processing tasks.
